examples.name: Default
examples.summary: The layer fills its nearest positioned ancestor, so the box it sits in is what gives it a size.

examples.name: Kinds
examples.summary: Five materials at their measured geometry. `dots` is the quiet default and `lines` the quietest — fine vertical rules whose transparency is the ink’s own, so each one stays solid edge to edge. `dither` ramps its density along an axis, and `pixelate` lights its grid from underneath with two crossing waves.

examples.name: Sizes
examples.summary: One step either side of the measured pitch. A size scales the texture whole, so the cell keeps its proportion to the lattice.

examples.name: Fades
examples.summary: The layer masks itself so it can meet copy without a hard edge. `--texture-fade-start` is where it still holds full ink and `--texture-fade-end` is where it reaches zero, so a band can steer the fade without re-writing the mask.
